newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Petron cancels tender to buy August gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Petron cancels tender to buy August gasoline.

text.p: Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp has cancelled its first gasoline import tender in about two years, because of "operational considerations", a company official said on Monday.
"The tender was cancelled," the official said. "We don't know yet whether a new tender will be issued."

The official did not elaborate on the reasons for the cancellation of the tender which sought 70,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for August 11-15 delivery, on a cost-and-freight basis to Bataan.
The tender closed on July 18 and was vaild for the day.
An official had said when the tender was issued that Petron went ahead with the decision to issue the import tender despite the de facto devaluation of the peso on July 11.
The peso, currently trading at $28.40 to the U.S. dollar compared to $26.40 when the central bank announced that it would allow the peso to trade in a wider band against the U.S. dollar.

Petron, which operates a 155,000-bpd refinery in Bataan, north of the capital Manila, had not issued an gasoline import tender since 1995 but had to re-emerge last week to buy due to increased domestic demand, an official had said.
But industry sources had also said the import requirement was also partly due to the unexpected shutdown of a 15,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) thermal cracker on June 20 following an explosion.
The unit, which produces diesel, gasoline and liquefied petroleum gas, is expected to be shut for about one month.
